name: Royal Palace, Luang Prabang
scope: Standing main royal palace (Haw Kham), now the Luang Prabang National Museum. Includes the mapped reception, throne and residential building wings, the front marble steps and the Lao gilded spire.
era: Standing former royal palace shown in the published 2006 original, currently operated as the National Museum.

references.caption: The former Royal Palace in Luang Phrabāng, now a museum
references.alt: The former Royal Palace in Luang Phrabāng, now a museum

originalReview.notes: Front-axis view shows the white pavilion and marble steps, deep-red wing roofs, low formal window band, gilded pediment and tall tiered gold throne-hall spire.

review.notes: Started with the two published Qualla public-domain candidates. Adam Carr’s vertical frontage original matches the native image and the documented author release. The other local file lacks a byte match to the current Commons original or an archived native revision, and was excluded. The palace uses the named current map and written museum documentation for the hidden ends.
